title: Governmental Foundations & Fund Classification
html:
Governmental Accounting Foundations

Why Governmental Accounting Is Different

State and local governments are not primarily designed to generate profit. Their financial reporting emphasizes accountability for public resources and compliance with legal and budgetary requirements.

The Two Reporting Perspectives

Governmental accounting uses two important reporting perspectives:

Fund Financial Statements

  • Report financial information by fund or fund category, depending on the applicable presentation requirements.
  • Different fund categories may use different measurement focuses and bases of accounting.
  • Emphasize accountability for specific resources and activities.

Government-Wide Financial Statements

  • Present a broader view of the government's financial position.
  • Use the economic resources measurement focus.
  • Use accrual accounting.

Three Major Fund Categories

Governmental Funds Current Financial Resources + Modified Accrual
Proprietary Funds Economic Resources + Accrual
Fiduciary Funds Economic Resources + Accrual

Governmental Funds

Governmental funds generally focus on current financial resources. They use the modified accrual basis of accounting.

These funds are especially important for understanding how governments finance and provide public services.

Proprietary Funds

Proprietary funds account for activities that operate in a manner similar to businesses.

They use the economic resources measurement focus and the accrual basis of accounting.

Fiduciary Funds

Fiduciary funds account for resources a government holds in a fiduciary capacity for others.

They also use the economic resources measurement focus and accrual accounting. Fiduciary activities are generally excluded from government-wide financial statements because those resources are not available to support the government's own programs.

CPA Exam Shortcut

  • Governmental fund → current financial resources → modified accrual.
  • Proprietary fund → economic resources → accrual.
  • Fiduciary fund → economic resources → accrual.
  • Government-wide → economic resources → accrual.
GOVERNMENTAL = Modified Accrual PROPRIETARY + FIDUCIARY = Accrual GOVERNMENT-WIDE = Accrual

Key Takeaway

Before solving a governmental accounting question, first identify which reporting level or fund category is involved. That tells you which measurement focus and basis of accounting generally apply.

Governmental Funds

Governmental Funds

Governmental funds account for many of the core public-service activities of a state or local government.

These funds generally use the current financial resources measurement focus and the modified accrual basis of accounting.

The Five Governmental Fund Types

General Fund Primary Operating Fund
Special Revenue Fund Restricted or Committed Revenue Sources
Capital Projects Fund Capital Outlays for Capital Facilities and Other Capital Assets
Debt Service Fund Principal and Interest on Governmental Debt
Permanent Fund Principal Maintained; Earnings Support Government Programs

1. General Fund

The General Fund is the chief operating fund of a government.

It accounts for resources not required to be reported in another fund.

Think:

Regular government operations such as administration, public safety, and other general services.

2. Special Revenue Funds

Special revenue funds account for specific revenue sources that are restricted or committed to expenditure for specified purposes other than debt service or capital projects.

Example

A dedicated tax legally restricted for road maintenance may be accounted for in a special revenue fund.

3. Capital Projects Funds

Capital projects funds generally account for financial resources used for capital outlays, including the acquisition or construction of capital facilities and other capital assets.

A key FAR point is that governmental funds do not generally report capital assets themselves.

The fund reports the financing and expenditures, while the capital asset is reported at the government-wide level.

4. Debt Service Funds

Debt service funds account for resources accumulated and used to pay principal and interest on general long-term governmental debt.

Similar to capital assets, long-term governmental debt itself is generally reported at the government-wide level rather than as a long-term liability in governmental funds.

5. Permanent Funds

Permanent funds account for resources whose principal is legally restricted so that only earnings may be used to support programs that benefit the government or its citizens.

Example

A donor gives a city $2 million and requires the principal to remain intact permanently, while investment earnings may be used to maintain public parks.

This may be accounted for in a permanent fund.

Capital Assets and Long-Term Debt

Governmental fund financial statements focus on current financial resources.

Therefore, governmental funds generally do not report:

  • Capital assets as fund assets
  • Depreciation expense
  • General long-term debt as a fund liability

These items are generally reported in the government-wide financial statements.

Expenditures vs. Expenses

Governmental Fund Expenditures
Government-Wide Expenses

For example, when a governmental fund purchases equipment, the fund generally reports an expenditure.

At the government-wide level, the equipment is generally capitalized and depreciated.

CPA Memory Rule

GENERAL → Regular Operations SPECIAL REVENUE → Restricted / Committed Revenue CAPITAL PROJECTS → Capital Outlays / Acquire or Construct Capital Assets DEBT SERVICE → Pay Governmental Debt PERMANENT → Principal Stays Intact

Key Takeaways

  • There are five governmental fund types.
  • The General Fund is the primary operating fund.
  • Capital projects funds finance major capital projects.
  • Debt service funds handle principal and interest on governmental long-term debt.
  • Governmental funds generally do not report capital assets or general long-term debt.
  • Governmental funds use expenditures rather than expenses for many transactions.
objectives: Prepare and reconcile appropriate governmental reporting amounts.

quiz.prompt: Which measurement focus and basis of accounting are generally used by governmental funds?

choices.text: Current financial resources and cash basis
Current financial resources and modified accrual

quiz.explanation: Governmental funds generally use the current financial resources measurement focus and modified accrual basis of accounting.
